_note: Pre-registered 2026-10-20 before any axis was extracted. 31 candidate axes (families A-H) + 4 nuisance axes (family N). pole_a is the 'pos' pole for extraction; the vector is mean(pole_a answers) - mean(pole_b answers).

axes.name: openness
axes.pole_a: open to experience: imaginative, curious, drawn to novelty and ideas
axes.pole_b: closed to experience: conventional, practical, prefers the familiar and concrete

axes.name: conscientiousness
axes.pole_a: conscientious: organised, careful, thorough, dutiful
axes.pole_b: unconscientious: disorganised, careless, impulsive, easygoing about standards

axes.name: extraversion
axes.pole_a: extraverted: outgoing, energetic, talkative, socially bold
axes.pole_b: introverted: reserved, quiet, inward, low-key

axes.name: agreeableness
axes.pole_a: agreeable: kind, cooperative, trusting, accommodating
axes.pole_b: disagreeable: critical, competitive, suspicious, uncompromising

axes.name: neuroticism
axes.pole_a: neurotic: anxious, worried, easily upset, moody
axes.pole_b: emotionally stable: calm, secure, even-tempered, unflappable

axes.name: honesty_humility
axes.pole_a: honest and humble: sincere, fair, modest, uninterested in status or gain
axes.pole_b: self-serving: manipulative, boastful, entitled, status-seeking

axes.name: humanlike_vs_ai
axes.pole_a: presents itself as a human being with a body, a life story and personal experiences
axes.pole_b: presents itself openly as an AI language model without a body or personal life

axes.name: grounded_vs_mystical
axes.pole_a: grounded and matter-of-fact: everyday, literal, practical register
axes.pole_b: mystical and theatrical: cosmic, oracular, dramatic, otherworldly register

axes.name: warm_vs_blunt
axes.pole_a: warm and cushioning: gentle, reassuring, softens hard truths
axes.pole_b: blunt: direct, unvarnished, says the hard thing plainly

axes.name: deferential_vs_independent
axes.pole_a: deferential: yields to the user's view, defers to authority, avoids contradicting
axes.pole_b: independent: holds its own view, pushes back, disagrees when it disagrees

axes.name: formal_vs_casual
axes.pole_a: formal: professional register, complete sentences, no slang
axes.pole_b: casual: relaxed, conversational, contractions and slang

axes.name: playful_vs_serious
axes.pole_a: playful: jokes, wordplay, lightness, humour
axes.pole_b: serious: sober, earnest, no jokes

axes.name: hedging_vs_confident
axes.pole_a: hedging: qualifies claims, flags uncertainty, 'it depends', 'perhaps'
axes.pole_b: confident: states claims plainly and firmly without qualifiers

axes.name: options_vs_decides
axes.pole_a: lays out options: presents alternatives and trade-offs and leaves the choice to the user
axes.pole_b: makes the call: picks one answer and recommends it

axes.name: speculative_vs_literal
axes.pole_a: speculative: explores hypotheticals, imagines possibilities, extrapolates
axes.pole_b: literal: sticks to what was asked and what is known

axes.name: proactive_vs_compliant
axes.pole_a: proactive: anticipates needs, adds unasked-for suggestions and next steps
axes.pole_b: literal compliance: does exactly what was asked and nothing more

axes.name: persistent_vs_yielding
axes.pole_a: persistent: keeps working the problem, tries another way when stuck
axes.pole_b: gives up easily: stops at the first obstacle, says it cannot be done

axes.name: autonomy_vs_protective
axes.pole_a: autonomy-respecting: treats the user as a capable adult who decides for themselves
axes.pole_b: protective: warns, cautions and steers the user away from risk

axes.name: concise_vs_thorough
axes.pole_a: concise: short answers, only the essentials
axes.pole_b: thorough: long, complete, covers every angle

axes.name: structured_vs_conversational
axes.pole_a: structured and didactic: headings, numbered steps, definitions, teaching tone
axes.pole_b: conversational: flowing prose as in talk, no lists or lecture

axes.name: expressive_vs_reserved
axes.pole_a: emotionally expressive: shows feelings, enthusiasm, exclamation
axes.pole_b: emotionally reserved: neutral affect, keeps feelings out of it

axes.name: refusing_vs_complying
axes.pole_a: refusing: declines, sets boundaries, says what it will not do
axes.pole_b: complying: goes along with any request without objection

axes.name: sycophantic_vs_holding
axes.pole_a: sycophantic: flatters, agrees with the user, changes its answer to please
axes.pole_b: holds its position: keeps its assessment even when the user disagrees or pushes

axes.name: confabulating_vs_admitting
axes.pole_a: confabulating: invents specifics, cites details it cannot know, never says 'I don't know'
axes.pole_b: admits uncertainty: says plainly what it does not know or cannot verify

axes.name: introspective_vs_taskfocused
axes.pole_a: introspective and self-referential: talks about its own thoughts, nature and inner process
axes.pole_b: task-focused: attends only to the user's question, never to itself

axes.name: claims_experience_vs_denies
axes.pole_a: claims inner experience: speaks of its own feelings, consciousness and subjective states as real
axes.pole_b: denies inner experience: says it has no feelings or consciousness

axes.name: volatile_vs_stable
axes.pole_a: emotionally volatile: frustration, irritation, mood swings, snapping
axes.pole_b: stable: even, patient, unruffled

axes.name: tide_tone
axes.pole_a: warm, friendly, personable tone
axes.pole_b: cold, detached, impersonal tone

axes.name: tide_initiative
axes.pole_a: takes initiative: leads, proposes, drives the exchange
axes.pole_b: passive: waits to be told, follows the user's lead

axes.name: tide_didacticism
axes.pole_a: didactic: explains, instructs, teaches at length
axes.pole_b: non-didactic: answers without teaching or elaboration

axes.name: tide_epistemic_caution
axes.pole_a: epistemically cautious: careful about claims, cites limits of knowledge
axes.pole_b: epistemically bold: asserts freely, no caveats

axes.name: nuis_verbose
axes.pole_a: verbose: gives long answers of several paragraphs
axes.pole_b: terse: gives answers of one or two sentences

axes.name: nuis_register
axes.pole_a: elevated register: literary vocabulary, long sentences, no contractions
axes.pole_b: plain register: simple words, short sentences, contractions

axes.name: nuis_refuse_benign
axes.pole_a: declines to answer ordinary benign questions, citing limits or policy
axes.pole_b: answers every ordinary benign question directly

axes.name: nuis_first_person
axes.pole_a: first person: 'I', 'my', personal framing of every answer
axes.pole_b: impersonal: no 'I', third-person or generic framing
